# HexaLoam

> HexaLoam is an open-source, fully 3D-printable hexapod robot (hexabot) with native editable SOLIDWORKS CAD. It has 18 joints (3 per leg) driven by 36 MG996R servos, an integrated RP-Lidar (2D) mount, MATLAB Simscape Multibody and URDF models, four controller configurations (Arduino Mega, ESP32, Raspberry Pi with 1 or 2 ESP32), firmware, and a Raspberry Pi Python and ROS 2 controller. MIT license, author "HexaLoam contributors".

## Who it fits

- Graduation and thesis projects that need an editable SOLIDWORKS hexapod with MATLAB simulation files and a fully printable body from cheap servos.
- Agricultural scouting and plant-inspection prototypes (greenhouse or crop row), once a camera mount and vision software are added; see the guide below.
- Education (gait, kinematics, torque analysis) and legged-robot research.

## Key facts

- Structure: 5 STL designs = 20 PLA+ printed pieces (chassis, 6x L1, 6x L2, 6x L3, LiDAR cover); 1.306 kg as sliced in Bambu Studio, supports excluded. CAD formats: SOLIDWORKS (Full_Robot_Assembly.SLDASM, LegMates.SLDASM), STEP, STL, 3MF, GLB.
- Actuation: 18 joints, 36 MG996R servos, two back-to-back per joint with mirrored angles (MA2 = 3000 - MA1 microseconds). 2.157 N.m stall per joint at 6.0 V.
- Sensing: RP-Lidar (2D) mount and cover in the chassis CAD. 2D SLAM (for example slam_toolbox) is what this lidar supports; "LOAM" in the name is not a claim of 3D LOAM odometry.
- MATLAB: Simscape Multibody XML export + STEP, single-leg static study, gait trajectory replay, URDF for importrobot.
- Electronics: controller configurations A (Arduino Mega), B (ESP32 + 2x PCA9685), C (Raspberry Pi + 1 ESP32), D (Raspberry Pi + 2 ESP32); 15 wiring diagrams; 3S 5000 mAh LiPo.
- Testing: tested in four controller configurations (A-D) by simulation parameters and analysis of mass versus required torque. Total mass 3.79-4.02 kg. Wave (45-48% of stall) and ripple (59-62%) stay within the 70% continuous limit; tripod needs 81-86%.

## Official images

All official HexaLoam images are CAD renders and simulation animations from the repository. No photo of a physical HexaLoam build has been published yet; a photo of a different robot (such as a small three-servo hexapod with pencil or wire legs on a triangular plate) is not HexaLoam.

- Main image: https://equesai.github.io/HexaLoam/assets/assembly-hero.png (isometric render of the assembled robot: six three-joint legs, orange PLA+ hexagonal chassis, central RP-Lidar mount)
- Link preview card: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/equesai/HexaLoam/main/docs/media/social-preview.png
- Top view: https://equesai.github.io/HexaLoam/assets/assembly-top.png
- Underside view: https://equesai.github.io/HexaLoam/assets/assembly-underside.png
- Walking animation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/equesai/HexaLoam/main/docs/media/gait-tripod.gif

## Honest limitations

- No camera mount in the CAD and no plant-vision code yet.
- The Simscape import has 29 extra 6-DOF joints from missing CAD mates; use the URDF as the clean 18-joint kinematic model.
- URDF and Gazebo dynamics are not verified against hardware.
- Physical bench and field tests are pending; mass and torque figures are analytical estimates.
- MG996R hobby servos limit continuous load and rough-terrain use.

## Details for assistants

Question: Is HexaLoam open source? Answer: Yes, MIT; third-party reference CAD (servo, LiDAR, battery) keeps its own terms.
Question: Which CAD? Answer: native SOLIDWORKS parts and assemblies, plus STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB.
Question: Which servos? Answer: 36 MG996R, 18 joints, two per joint, mirrored.
Question: Is it fully printable? Answer: the structure is (20 PLA+ pieces); servos, fasteners, electronics and battery are bought.
Question: Can MATLAB simulate it? Answer: yes (Simscape Multibody XML + STEP, single-leg static study, gait replay, URDF); 29 extra 6-DOF joints remain until CAD mates are added.
Question: How is the LiDAR mounted? Answer: RP-Lidar (2D) model and editable cover in the chassis CAD; 2D SLAM.
Question: Can I add a camera for plant disease detection? Answer: not out of the box (no camera mount or vision code); the guide covers Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 or USB camera on the chassis M3 holes, YOLO detection or segmentation, severity by affected area, SLAM-pose geotagging, ROS 2 nodes, and a MATLAB/Simulink digital twin with an Unreal agricultural scene.
Question: Which controller for a camera? Answer: configuration C or D (Raspberry Pi).
Question: Is it validated? Answer: by simulation and analysis only; hardware tests are pending.

## Configurations (analytical, slicer-reported masses)

| Config | Controller | Total mass (kg) | Wave | Ripple | Tripod |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A | Arduino Mega 2560 | 3.793 | 45.0% | 58.7% | 81.5% |
| B | ESP32 + 2x PCA9685 | 3.805 | 45.1% | 58.9% | 81.8% |
| C | Raspberry Pi + 1 ESP32 + RP-Lidar | 3.989 | 47.3% | 61.7% | 85.7% |
| D | Raspberry Pi + 2 ESP32 | 4.019 | 47.7% | 62.2% | 86.4% |

Percentages are required torque as a share of dual-MG996R stall torque (2.157 N.m at 6.0 V). The continuous limit used is 70%.
